lines.en: Well, that was weird.
Time to completely ignore it and become a student for the sake of sport.
: So it was only for a few seconds? And she went right back to acting normal?
: Yeah. It was like some kind of...eggy switch flipped inside of her all of a sudden. And no, I already ruled out drugs.
: Bitch, of course Ayane ain’t doing drugs. Sounds like some kind of PTSD thing. Just don’t bring up eggs around her at all anymore and see how things go.
: Like...all of them?
: Are eggs a frequent conversation topic of yours?
: Maybe at diners.
: And do you plan on going to a diner with Amamiya?
: If she asks, maybe.
: Ahem.
: What do you want? You’re supposed to raise your hand if you have something to say.
: I’m just trying to subtly recall the last five minutes so I can figure out how I got here.
: Just so we’re all on the same page, I haven’t ruled out drugs for Akira yet.
: We should give him some. They might fix him.
: Only your love can fix me, Wakana.
: Somebody gonna tell Niki that? We’ll probably have a good shot later tonight when she forcibly inserts herself into our circle again.
: Aren’t you the one who invited her?
: Yes, but there’s a perfectly good explanation for that. I thought it’d make her like you less.
: I can promise you there is nothing you can do to make her like me less. Trust me, I have tried.
: Where is she, by the way? The only chance I ever got to speak with her was during the beach trip where the two of you cuckolded Imani.
: They did not cuckold me, Wakana! Senpai and I weren’t even a thing yet!
: He and I definitely cuckolded you, though. It still counts if the cuck is asleep, right?
: Okay, that time definitely counts! And thank you for reminding me, Rika! I needed that!
: Hey, I’m just saying, if it’s happened two times now, maybe you’re just into it?
: Just because a shitty thing keeps happening to me doesn’t mean that I-
: Um...I’m sorry for interrupting, but...I think you may have forgotten about us?
: Thank you for raising your hand, Fukuyama. And yes, we certainly did.
: I didn’t forget, Futaba. I just have no reason to hide anything from you since I love you so much and I know that you love me too and will acknowledge the romantic pickle I am in right now.
: Bitch, you locked yourself in the damn jar. It ain’t just one pickle anymore, it’s a whole sea of them.
: Hey, that’s probably more action than Wakana’s gotten in months.
: As the one rational adult here, I suppose I’ll take the lead and remind the two of you less rational ones that these matters should be reserved for outside of school.
: You tell them, Wakana.
: Arakawa, please die in a fire so I no longer have to remember you are here.
: Is it just me, or is this competition shaping up to be yet another nonsensical bout of unwanted chaos and future regret?
: It would be helpful to at least...know what we’re doing exactly.
: Well said. It appears that you and I are the most mature women in the room.
: I mean, if we’re going off of physical traits...
: Y’all gotta be cheatin’ the system looking like that. Girls were way smaller back in the day. They putting something in the water now?
: The “day” for you was rather recent, wasn’t it? You’ve only been out of college a handful of years.
: Those years’ll hit you like a truck if you let them, Wakana.
: Have you tried maybe...not letting them?
: So, should Futaba and I just make up our own rules or do the three of you intend to actually tell them to us?
: I will say that it is kind of weird how urgently you were texting me if we were just going to stand around like we’re at the bar again.
: The rules are pretty straightforward, Touka. Us four adults are going to travel back in time for thirty minutes or so in an effort to recapture our youth.
: You don’t want me recapturing my youth in front of the students. I’d need to take Akira under the bleachers and who knows when he’d ever get back.
: Okaaaaay...then let’s just say the four of us will go sit at our desks and put our respective educations in the hands of you guys.
: Is there a specific subject or anything that we’re expected to teach? Or is it just...some sort of free-for-all?
: The topic can be anything you like as we believe it’s best for the two of you to express your abilities in the fields that you’re most comfortable.
: We will be asking questions, though. So don’t get thrown off by any of them if they have nothing to do with what you were talking about!
: You’re still high from the trivia thing, aren’t you?
: Ding dong. Oh, look. It’s the bell. Which means class is now in session and anyone not seated in the next thirty seconds is being expelled.
: You don’t have to tell me twice. Sitting down is probably my favorite hobby right after things like sleeping or talking myself off of a ledge.
: When the hell did you have time to make that? That tea wasn’t there a second ago.
: Akira, hi! Looks like we’re seat-mates! You don’t mind if I scooch a little closer, do you? I forgot my textbook and I need to share.
: But we don’t even know if there is a textbook yet.
: Pleeeeeease? I get really lonely if-
: Rika Rokuhara.
: Here!
: Oh, right. I guess we should take attendance. Umm...
: A...Akira Arakawa?...
: Hello.
: Akira Arakawa?
: Still here.
: Touka?
: Presen- oh. Reflex. And sorry for the repetition. I just wanted to try saying his name in this context too. But seeing as we have now both had our fun, this leaves...Wakana Watabe?
: Present.
: And..Imani Imai?
: Also present! And might I say, the two of you are looking absolutely stunning today.
: Flattery will get you nowhere, Imai-san. Only the most insidious teacher alive would feed into or allow such open depravity.
: Despicable. I can’t believe I left my class in the hands of this woman.
: That wasn’t a pick-up line! I was just-

: Fukuyama-sensei, what do you think about divvying up the class and handling two students each? Studies show that the more time a teacher spends with their students, the more likely they are to succeed.
: Ahh, so that’s why 1-A has been the highest scoring class since before Imani even showed up.
: All I’ve ever wanted to do is help this nation’s youth.
: Uhh...splitting them up is fine. I’ll take Miss Imai and Miss Watabe. And-
: And leave me with the two delinquents? Is this an admission that you’re scared of instructing them and believe you’d fare better pawning them off on me instead?
: It...wasn’t on purpose. But I imagine it...might have been subconscious?
: I haven’t even done anything yet and I’m already a delinquent. I wonder if this is how Yumi feels?
: Yumi beat a girl half to death in the middle of a school day.
: Yes, but it was Nagasawa so she probably had it coming.
: It’s been ages since I last heard her utter my name. Coming here is already worth it.
: I only remember because of the restraining order that’s been sitting on my desk for months that I’ve been too busy to file.
: Futabaaaaa! Teach them stuuuuuuuuff!
: Excuse me, but if the two of you are not members of this class, I’ll have to ask you to leave now.
: We got prior approval, actually. But I believe there was a “no cheering” section on the application, so I’m going to go ahead and get right back to shutting up now.
: Wow! Does everybody else see that super cute girl off to the side of the room?
: Everyone but Akira. He should just look outside of the window or something.
: Yeah, so take this and multiply it by a bunch and that’s basically what I experience every single day.
: I can only imagine...I never assumed this would be easy, though. And...maybe I should have prepared more, but I’m not really sure what I can teach you that you don’t already know.

: It’s fine if we know something already. We’re just here to evaluate your teaching ability. In fact, it’s probably better if you “teach” us something we already know so we can hear how you explain it.
: How about literature? You looked up to Senpai before I got here, right? That was his field of expertise. And I know you read a lot too.
: Well, yes...but the books I’ve been reading lately aren’t exactly fit for school. And I’m even worse at writing, so...
: Chin up. And fake confidence if you can’t find it. Once a teacher shows weakness, their students will jump all over it.
: I guess that explains Arakawa’s popularity too.
: Do you choose violence the moment you get out of bed or is it my face that spurs you to action?
: It comes naturally. It’s not really a conscious thing.
: Arakawa-kun, please pay attention in class. I’ve been standing here for almost a minute now and you’ve yet to even look at me.
: Oh, sorry. I’m just not really used to being on this end of the educational process.
: I’m not used to being on any end of it. I just turn on the metronome for Sana once a day and collect a paycheck. I’m one of those “essential worker” things I think.
: Very close, Rokuhara-san. You see, teachers are considered essential workers. But society would not collapse if you forgot to turn on a metronome. There are plenty of people to fill that role.

: Take Arakawa-kun for example. If you ignore the fact that he’s still collecting a paycheck from the school during his impossibly long sabbatical, he appears more or less the same as any other unemployed man out there.

: Surely he could turn on a metronome. It requires no skill at all. But instead, he refuses to provide any relief whatsoever to the city’s labor shortage by remaining in his bed and staring at the ceiling all day.
: I just want to make sure it isn’t going anywhere.

: Arakawa-kun, did you know that over 1%% of the population of Japan is estimated to be hikikomori — or those who self-isolate for extended periods of time to avoid all social contact in fear of shame or failure?
: I can’t tell if I’m learning things or just getting called out here.
: Who says it can’t be both? One of the most tried and true ways to learn anything is through personal experience.
: And just because you’re a failure now doesn’t mean you have to be so long as you try to overcome it and get better. You don’t want to be some sort of statistic, do you, Arakawa-kun?
: Not really. But I also don’t want to do anything either. And I am perfectly capable of feeling ashamed from the comfort of my own home.
: Right you are. And it is that mindset that leads to situations like Rokuhara-san pressing a button and then deeming herself essential.
: Those with talent should use it. And I know you’re capable. So the fact that you’re not using it makes me think you just need someone to believe in you. Like me, for example.
: Can I have a compliment now? Akira’s getting to hear all this nice stuff and all I’m hearing is that my job is going to be replaced by AI.
: With all due respect, your job should probably just not even exist.
Seeing the two of them like this...and hearing from Touka that I’m wasting my talent makes me kind of miss being a teacher for the moment.
I know I left because I figured it’s what was best for everyone, but...maybe in another world, I stuck around and toughed it out.
I mean, it’s not like all of my alone time has made me any better of a person. And, in a lot of ways, I might actually be worse because it really is like I’m just not contributing at all anymore.
I think if I ever did come back, I’d try a little harder. I wouldn’t just confine myself to the space behind a desk while waiting for the bell to ring each day.

And, if I ever did, I’d have Imani to back me up. Wakana too. Even Rika who, despite not being a teacher, is still a great friend. There are so many people in this building that support me and want me to succeed.

Yet my inaction and failure to do anything with that knowledge is but one more testament to my affinity for solitary confinement. How I’m at ease when things are easy. How hard it is to leave the room.
And how things like that are just as true for girls like Futaba. But there she is, smiling and doing her best because she wants to be better and doesn’t want to be like me.
I won’t take credit for this. I imagine this is all Imani’s doing. Or something that falls from the hands that try to hold her up.
But whatever it is, I’m envious. Of the joy. How her hands should be shaking but aren’t. Meanwhile, mine are tucked beneath the desk so no one can see them.

She spends the class explaining the differences in fantasy subgenres to Imani and Wakana, who do a great job of feigning interest. Or maybe they just are interested? I don’t know. I can’t see inside of their minds.
But if I could, I’d look around in hopes that they cherish this moment. That they see how big it is and how far she’s come from the quiet girl in the library I met so many years ago.

Touka’s strategy stays more or less the same with pointing out my and Rika’s flaws, but there’s much more emphasis put on facts and how to turn them around than there is beating around the bush or sugarcoating our inadequacies.
I can’t tell if she lucked out with students like us or if this works against her in some way. Nor can I tell if what she’s doing is actually inspirational or not.
But it got me thinking. Seriously thinking. And that’s more than most things do lately.
So perhaps her goal wasn’t to be a motivator so much as it was to cause some self-reflection.
Because yeah, some people are just talented. And watching them waste all that away won’t ever feel good if you really do believe in them.
It makes me wonder if this comes from a place of personal experience or just the desire to experience such things. Because I still don’t know if my approach with her was right or not.
She hated me at first...but look at us now. Look at the holes I’ve carved in her heart and how love oozes from each and every septal defect until the two of us are bathed in it.
Is that enough, though? Enough to make me move. Or would she rather I just stay?
I feel like she’d answer if I asked her.
But, as always...
I can not find the strength.
: Alright, gang. That’s a full hour worth of learning and I am pleased to say that, despite several early distractions, this contest was definitely not a trainwreck.
: I imagine that just means the obstacle course will be, though. So RIP Wakana, I guess.
: But anyway, how’d you guys feel about teaching? Any new career plans going forward? Has this one day changed the entire trajectory of your lives?

: Not in the slightest. I did enjoy being able to constructively criticize Sensei in a controlled environment, though. It was like being able to throw tomatoes at him while he’s locked behind bars. Quite nice, really.
: I...didn’t exactly have the same experience. I did have fun, though.
: I don’t know if this will, like...change anything about my future, but...I don’t know. I don’t really have anything I specifically want to do yet anyway, so...
: We’ll see...
: Well, the original plan here was for me to be the judge of this contest...but seeing as Senpai was equally as involved, perhaps he and I should collaborate?
: You’re just torn because you like both of them and need me to break the tie, don’t you?
: Kinda, yeah.
I had a feeling things would come to this. But I’d already made up my mind before I was even asked...
And my choice for who the best teacher out of these two would be is...
Futaba
: In that case, I have to give it to Futaba.
: R-Really?! I...actually beat Touka? She’s...so much smarter than me, though.
: Touka wasn’t bad by any means. I just don’t think the style she employed today would jive with most people — especially ones your age.
: Futaba, you have a lot to learn still, but your more traditional methods and soft demeanor would make you a great teacher for younger kids.
: Your presence is comforting and calming and your passion was clearly evident even if you spent most of your time with Imani and Wakana.
: Th...Thank you, Sensei! That really means a lot to me. And...congratulations to you too, Touka. Even if you didn’t win.
: I could have sworn you had me beat when I started hearing you throw out a bunch of numbers and stuff...hahah...
: Oh, yes. Congratulations to you, Futaba. You were quite exceptional yourself.
: Nothing else to add from the losing side?
: No. I’ve said my piece already. And even if I did not win, I think the weight of my words today will still make an impact.
: And if the point of teaching is to touch lives or bring out the best in someone, then...
: I suppose we’ll just have to wait and see if I make any difference at all.
Touka
: In that case, I have to give it to Touka.
: Though, I will say I don’t think her strategy would be best for everyone. And that pointing out the flaws in people can do more harm than good if they aren’t ready to hear them.
: Perhaps you should take your own advice then, Sensei. You weren’t all that reserved with me when I first arrived either, were you?
: No, I most certainly was not. But I think you turned out okay. Which means the two of us might be a little more similar than you thought.
: Oh, no. How horrible that would be.
: Is it just me or is the vibe here getting kinda weird all of a sudden?
: Congratulations, Touka. I kind of knew you’d win, but it was still fun regardless.
: It was, wasn’t it? And might I say, Futaba, I had no idea there were so many types of fantasy novels. So while you may not have won, you certainly taught me something.
: Really? That’s great. I’d be...happy to give you some recommendations if you ever drop by the library.
: I’ll see if I can make the time. I’d love to share some recommendations of my own with you too, if that’s okay. I’m not particularly well-versed in fantasy, but-
: Sorry, Touka. Futaba only reads books with elf-sex in them.
: Oh. Well...I don’t think I know of any books like that.
: S-Sensei! No I don’t! I read other books! In fact, most of the books I read don’t have anything like that!
: She’s lying to you, Touka. It’s the only thing she’s interested in.
: Man, if you just spoiled a potential friendship with your weird elf-sex thing, I’m gonna be pissed as Hell.
: I have interests other than elf-sex!!!!
: “Other” would imply that...it is an interest, though...yes?
: That...I...
: I...don’t want to say!
: She loves it. Just look at her.
: Aaaaaaaahhhhhhhhhh!!!!!!!
: Okay, okay! That’s seven contests down and three to go!
: We’ve got one more at the school before we head over to Koi Cafe for the barista war, so if everyone could now make their way over to the gym for the obstacle course, it would be-
